Step 1 — The idea
One way to construct such a function is to start with a continuous curve (the first property) with a stationary point at \(x={{CT:0}}\) and then to "bend" the curve at the point at which we need differentiability to fail. This can be done using the absolute value function \(|x|\).
Step 2 — Bending a quadratic
We start with a quadratic with roots at \(x=0\) and \(x=2\times {{CT:0}}\) which has a stationary point at the required \(x={{CT:0}}\). For example \(x(x-{{CT:1}})\). Now we can "bend" it with the absolute value function as follows:
